name: slack
description: Let your agent use Slack two ways: as a bot app you add to channels, or as you through your own account. Connect one or both.

ai.insodimension.dimension.title: Slack
examples: Post a message to #general as the bot letting the team know the deploy is done
Search Slack for what we decided about the launch date and summarize it
Draft a reply to Priya's message in the thread, show it to me, and send it as me once I approve

methods.label: A Slack bot app
methods.detail: Posts as a bot app you add to channels, and takes a bot token you paste in.

setup.title: Create a Slack app
setup.detail: At api.slack.com/apps click "Create New App" → "From scratch", give it a name (e.g. "Dimension"), and pick the workspace you want it to act in.

setup.title: Add Bot Token Scopes
setup.detail: In your app: OAuth & Permissions → Scopes → Bot Token Scopes → add channels:read, groups:read, channels:history, groups:history, and chat:write. These let the bot list channels, read history, and post. To let it upload files too, also add files:write.

setup.title: Install the app to your workspace
setup.detail: OAuth & Permissions → Install App → Install to Workspace → Allow. This generates the bot token.

setup.title: Copy the Bot User OAuth Token
setup.detail: Still on OAuth & Permissions, copy the "Bot User OAuth Token" (it starts with xoxb-) and paste it into the form below. It stays on this machine. Note: invite the bot into any channel with /invite before it can read or post there.

form.label: Bot User OAuth Token
form.help: From your Slack app's OAuth & Permissions page (starts with xoxb-). Install the app to your workspace first to generate it.

failures.title: Reconnect Slack — the bot token is invalid or revoked
failures.detail: Reinstall the app to your workspace and paste the fresh xoxb- token.

failures.title: Add the missing bot scopes
failures.detail: OAuth & Permissions → Bot Token Scopes → add channels:read, channels:history, chat:write — then reinstall the app.

methods.label: As you
methods.detail: Searches, reads and sends in your own name through Slack's official MCP server, and needs your own Slack app.

assist.label: Set up with your agent
assist.prompt:
Help me connect Slack as me, using the Browser plugin. I want to stay in control of every sign-in and approval.

Rules:
- Never ask for, read, type or reveal a password, a 2FA code or the app's Client Secret. If Slack needs me to sign in, open the sign-in page in the Browser view and wait for me to finish.
- Say what you are about to do before each step, and take a screenshot after it so I can follow along. Use browser_view so I can watch.
- If a page does not match what I describe, observe it and adapt. If you are unsure, ask me. If Slack blocks a step (admin approval, a workspace policy), stop and tell me exactly what it says. Do not retry or work around it.

Steps:
1. Call browser_profiles. If a saved profile is already signed in to Slack, ask me whether to use it. Otherwise open a new profile at https://slack.com/signin, ask me to sign in to the workspace I want, and wait.
2. Open this link. It opens Slack's Create an app dialog with Dimension's app manifest already filled in (user permissions to read and send as me, MCP on, PKCE on, redirect http://localhost:53682/callback):
https://api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_json=%7B%22display_information%22%3A%7B%22name%22%3A%22Dimension%20(as%20you)%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22Lets%20your%20Dimension%20agent%20read%20and%20send%20Slack%20messages%20as%20you%2C%20through%20Slack's%20MCP%20server.%22%7D%2C%22oauth_config%22%3A%7B%22redirect_urls%22%3A%5B%22http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A53682%2Fcallback%22%5D%2C%22scopes%22%3A%7B%22user%22%3A%5B%22canvases%3Aread%22%2C%22canvases%3Awrite%22%2C%22channels%3Ahistory%22%2C%22channels%3Aread%22%2C%22channels%3Awrite%22%2C%22chat%3Awrite%22%2C%22emoji%3Aread%22%2C%22files%3Aread%22%2C%22files%3Awrite%22%2C%22groups%3Ahistory%22%2C%22groups%3Aread%22%2C%22groups%3Awrite%22%2C%22im%3Ahistory%22%2C%22im%3Aread%22%2C%22im%3Awrite%22%2C%22lists%3Aread%22%2C%22lists%3Awrite%22%2C%22mpim%3Ahistory%22%2C%22mpim%3Aread%22%2C%22mpim%3Awrite%22%2C%22reactions%3Aread%22%2C%22reactions%3Awrite%22%2C%22search%3Aread.files%22%2C%22search%3Aread.im%22%2C%22search%3Aread.mpim%22%2C%22search%3Aread.private%22%2C%22search%3Aread.public%22%2C%22search%3Aread.users%22%2C%22users%3Aread%22%2C%22users%3Aread.email%22%5D%7D%2C%22pkce_enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22settings%22%3A%7B%22org_deploy_enabled%22%3Afalse%2C%22socket_mode_enabled%22%3Afalse%2C%22token_rotation_enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22is_mcp_enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%7D
3. Choose the workspace I name (ask me if there is more than one), click Next, check that the summary shows the user scopes and no errors, then click Create.
4. On the new app's Basic Information page, find App Credentials and read ONLY the Client ID (it looks like 1234567890.1234567890123). Do not open or copy the Client Secret.
5. Give me the Client ID and tell me what to do next: open Plugins, choose Slack, click Connect, pick As you, paste the Client ID, pick Read and send, and click Allow when Slack asks. If Slack says an admin must approve the app, tell me who to ask.
6. Close the browser tab you opened.

setup.title: Create the Slack app (one click)
setup.detail: This opens Slack's Create an app screen with everything filled in: the permissions to read and send as you, MCP switched on, PKCE on, and the localhost sign-in address. Pick your workspace, click Next, then Create.

setup.title: Get it approved, if Slack asks
setup.detail: Some workspaces make you ask an admin before an app can sign anyone in. If Slack says so, send them the app's page and wait. Dimension cannot get around that.

setup.title: Copy the Client ID
setup.detail: On the app's Basic Information page, under App Credentials, copy the Client ID. It is not a secret, and you do not need the Client Secret.

setup.title: Paste it below, choose what Dimension may do, and click Connect
setup.detail: Slack opens in your browser: click Allow. Port 53682 must be free while you connect. If this sign-in goes unused for about 30 days Slack can sign it out; click Connect again.

form.label: Client ID
form.help: From your Slack app's Basic Information page, under App Credentials. It is not a secret.

form.label: Client Secret (leave blank)
form.help: Leave this blank. The app uses PKCE, which needs no secret. Fill it in only if Slack rejects the connection with bad_client_secret.

scopeOptions.label: Read only
scopeOptions.detail: Search and read channels, threads, DMs, files, canvases and lists. Nothing can be sent.

scopeOptions.label: Read and send
scopeOptions.detail: Everything above, plus sending and scheduling messages and adding reactions, as you. In Ask and Write mode every send asks you first (Always allow on the card stops it asking for the rest of that session); in Full access nothing asks.

scopeOptions.label: Everything
scopeOptions.detail: Adds creating channels, writing canvases and lists, and uploading files.

failures.title: Reconnect Slack (as you)
failures.detail: Slack no longer accepts the saved sign-in. Click Connect again and allow access.

failures.title: Your workspace has not approved this app
failures.detail: Ask a workspace admin to approve the Dimension app, then click Connect again.

tools.name: slack_list_channels
tools.description: List public and private channels in the connected Slack workspace. Returns id/#name/topic per line; paginate with the returned cursor.

tools.name: slack_read_messages
tools.description: Read recent messages from a Slack channel (most-recent first). Returns ts/user/text per line — ts is the message id.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.description: Post a message to a Slack channel. Sends a real message: post only what was asked for. Returns the posted ts + channel.

tools.name: slack_read_thread
tools.description: Read the replies in a Slack thread (oldest first). Pass the parent message's ts as threadTs. Returns ts/user/text per line.

tools.name: slack_reply_thread
tools.description: Reply inside a Slack thread. Sends a real message: reply only with what was asked for. Returns the reply ts + channel.

tools.name: slack_add_reaction
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction to a message (emoji name without colons, e.g. thumbsup). Requires the reactions:write scope.

tools.name: slack_edit_message
tools.description: Edit a Slack message the bot posted (chat.update). Replaces the visible text: edit only what was asked for.

tools.name: slack_delete_message
tools.description: Delete a Slack message (chat.delete). It cannot be undone: delete only the exact message that was asked for.

tools.name: slack_upload_file
tools.description: Upload a file from the session's folder to a Slack channel as the bot, optionally with a message and in a thread. Shares a real file: upload only what was asked for. Needs the files:write bot scope.

tools.name: slack_list_users
tools.description: List workspace members. Returns id/@name/real name per line (deleted + bots flagged). Requires the users:read scope.

tools.name: slack_tools
tools.description: List what Slack's official MCP server can do for you, or describe one tool in full. Each tool is marked read or write.

tools.name: slack_read
tools.description: Run one read-only Slack tool as you: search, read a channel or thread, find users and channels, read a canvas.

tools.name: slack_act
tools.description: Run one Slack tool that changes Slack as you: send, schedule, react, create. DESTRUCTIVE: in Ask and Write mode you are asked to approve each call (Always allow on the card waives that for the rest of the session); in Full access nothing asks.
